questions.stem: A reaction profile shows reactants at 100 kJ, a peak at 180 kJ, and products at 40 kJ. What is the activation energy for the reverse reaction?
questions.explanation: The activation energy for the reverse reaction is measured from the products to the peak: Ea(reverse) = 180 - 40 = 140 kJ. The reverse reaction has a higher activation energy than the forward reaction (180 - 100 = 80 kJ) because this is an exothermic forward reaction.

questions.stem: What is the transition state (activated complex) on a reaction profile?

options.text: The energy level of the products
The point where the reactants are first mixed
The highest energy point where old bonds are partially broken and new bonds are partially formed
The point where the reaction reaches equilibrium

questions.explanation: The transition state (or activated complex) is the highest energy point on the reaction profile. At this point, the old bonds in the reactants are partially broken and the new bonds in the products are partially formed. It is an unstable arrangement that exists only momentarily.
